item.title: Wall Street Week | Affordability, Data Center Divide, Debt Hits Households, Capitalism on the Ballot
item.description: This week, a special edition of Wall Street Week as Americans head to the polls for midterm elections. Could affordability decide who controls Congress? And, voters may not agree on AI but opposition to new data centers is cutting across party lines. Plus, America’s growing debt burden is pushing up borrowing costs for the government and potentially thousands of dollars onto household finances. Later, are voters rejecting capitalism or simply looking for better solutions to rising costs? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Ramps Up Criminal Probe Amid Tight Alaska Senate Race
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Pat Toomey, former Pennsylvania Republican Senator, former ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee and Coinbase global advisory council member, says Republicans are in a "really rough spot" in the House while control of the Senate remains much more of an open question. Jessica Killin, Colorado Democratic Congressional candidate, says affordability is the central concern she hears from voters and argues Congress needs to take back its power on tariffs and the war with Iran. Jessica Taylor, Senate and Governors editor for The Cook Political Report, says President Donald Trump is needed on the campaign trail to drive Republican turnout, but making the midterms about himself could also motivate Democrats and independents to vote against his party. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: AI Trade Unwinds (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Wall Street got a reality check as a bruising selloff in technology shares fueled concern the artificial-intelligence frenzy that has powered the equity bull market might be overblown. Disappointing tech results spurred the worst drop for stocks since June, with the Nasdaq 100 briefly crossing the threshold of a technical correction. The index sank 3.5% Friday.
On today's episode:
Kristine Aquino, Bloomberg News Markets Live Blog Managing Editor Jeff Sprecher, Intercontinental Exchange CEO Muyao Shen, Bloomberg News Crypto Reporter Dan Sheridan, Brooks Running CEO (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Can Drive Turnout on Both Sides: Taylor
item.description: Jessica Taylor, Senate and Governors editor for The Cook Political Report, says President Donald Trump is needed on the campaign trail to drive Republican turnout, but making the midterms about himself could also motivate Democrats and independents to vote against his party. Taylor says Cook moved Florida's Senate race from Solid Republican to Likely Republican because it expects a single-digit contest and says Florida could offer an early indication of how Republicans are performing nationally. Taylor says some states could produce different results in their gubernatorial and Senate races and that the bigger question in the closing days is which voters ultimately turn out. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Killin Says Affordability Is Driving Colorado Race
item.description: Jessica Killin, Colorado Democratic Congressional candidate, says affordability is the central concern she hears from voters and argues Congress needs to take back its power on tariffs and the war with Iran. Killin says tariffs are raising costs for small businesses and calls for Congress to play a larger role in pursuing a longer-term agreement with Iran while also addressing housing and health care. Killin says her Army and private-sector background gives her an understanding of how to help the economy grow and calls questions over her Colorado residency a nonissue after a judge dismissed the case. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Toomey Says House in 'Really Rough Spot' for GOP
item.description: Pat Toomey, former Pennsylvania Republican Senator, former ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee and Coinbase global advisory council member, says Republicans are in a "really rough spot" in the House while control of the Senate remains much more of an open question. Toomey says the AI buildout should be assessed company by company because businesses have vastly different exposure to AI and it remains unclear where the economic gains ultimately will accrue. Toomey says Sherrod Brown returning to the Senate would be "unfortunate" for crypto and argues Brown has shown hostility toward business and crypto. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UN Peace Mission to Western Sahara Hits Unprecedented Standoff
item.description: The United Nations failed to renew the mandate of its peacekeeping mission to the disputed Western Sahara for the first time in 35 years, threatening to escalate tensions between Morocco and Sahrawi rebels fighting for an independent state in the territory.
item.dc:creator: Souhail Karam and Magdalena Del Valle

item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. item.title: Guyana Seeks Regional Support Ahead of Venezuela Border Ruling
item.description: Guyana is looking to shore up regional support ahead of an expected International Court of Justice ruling on its border dispute with Venezuela over the resource-rich Essequibo region.

item.title: Wall Street Punishes Tech Stocks on Earnings Misses
item.description: Wall Street got a reality check as a bruising selloff in technology shares fueled concern the artificial-intelligence frenzy that has powered the equity bull market might be overblown. Disappointing tech results spurred the worst drop for stocks since June, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 3.5% and briefly crossing the threshold of a technical correction. Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King, Bloomberg News Technology Reporter Matt Day and Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Technology Analyst Anurag Rana join to recap Intel and Amazon earnings. Plus, Jeff Sprecher, Intercontinental Exchange CEO joins to discuss the company's deal with Hyperliquid to bring perpetual futures products into US markets. Then, Bloomberg News Senior Equities Editor Eric Weiner helps dissect today's major selloff. Finally, Brooks Running CEO Dan Sheridan joins ahead of the New York City Marathon to discuss the shoe company's market share and customer demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House to Nominate Mufarrige to FTC Commissioner Spot
item.description: The White House is poised to nominate Christopher Mufarrige to the US Federal Trade Commission, according to people familiar with the administration’s plans, elevating him from leading the consumer protection division to become one of the agency’s top policymakers.

item.description: The Trump administration approved a $2.1 billion sale of Patriot missiles to Ukraine, after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the US of delaying shipments of the crucial air defense interceptors.

item.description: When Indian police closed in on young protesters in New Delhi this month, Simran locked hands with a friend. They made a quick pact: if they were getting hauled away, they were going together.
